findings.issue_text: [BUG] EmailValidator lives under lib/ but User references it via validates with no explicit require; if lib/ is not in autoload paths, loading User in production raises ArgumentError: Unknown validator: 'EmailValidator', breaking every code path that loads the User model

[ADVISORY] should_block? performs a record.save (write plus UPDATE on every match) from inside EmailValidator#validate_each within the User model's validation phase, causing extra writes inside the User transaction; blocked-email counters/last_match_at roll back with the user save or update under contention, making stats silently wrong
[ADVISORY] Counter increments race (read-modify-write with no increment_counter), so concurrent signups lose counts

[ADVISORY] BlockedEmails table and model are added with no writer anywhere in the diff (no admin UI, rake task, seed, or console-documented path inserts rows), making the blocking feature dead code in production

[ADVISORY] Domain-restriction regex logic moved into the validator is now only reachable via validates ... if: :email_changed? on the User model; code paths referencing the now-deleted email_in_restriction_setting? method on User break, and whitelist/blacklist enforcement is coupled to the email_changed? guard on a single model, so callers validating emails outside a User record get no enforcement unless they remember the if: condition

[ADVISORY] Ships-inert feature: nothing in this diff writes to blocked_emails — no admin UI, API endpoint, rake task, seed, or importer inserts BlockedEmail records, so operators cannot actually block any email address and should_block? always returns false in deployed environments.

[ADVISORY] Coverage gap for moved logic: whitelist/blacklist restriction behavior moved from user.rb into the new EmailValidator, but the new spec stubs should_block? and tests nothing else — no test exercises a whitelist or blacklist setting through the validator, so regressions in regex-building or elsif precedence are caught by no test.

[ADVISORY] Hidden coupling: EmailValidator in lib/ hard-depends on the BlockedEmail model, executing DB reads and writes (match_count increment, last_match_at update, save) from inside validate_each on every email validation, even when action_type is :do_nothing or the email later fails uniqueness, inflating match counts.

[ADVISORY] Exact-string case-sensitive matching on the rejected-email client guard and the server's BlockedEmail.where(email:) lookup means users rejected with one casing can retry with different casing to bypass blocks, and admins who load the table without downcasing see blocks silently not enforced.

[BUG] rejectedEmails is only populated when result.errors.email is present, and when a blocked email is paired with other errors the user sees the generic 'user.email.invalid' message instead of the distinct 'user.email.blocked' locale string this diff adds but never uses on the client.

[ADVISORY] Gating-condition change without verification: the blocked check runs only when email_changed?, and alternate account-creation/claim paths (admin-created users, OmniAuth, invites) that set email without going through users#create never get the blocked check exercised by any spec, so the stated goal is enforced only on the one tested controller path.

[ADVISORY] app/models/blocked_email.rb:9-16 — `should_block?` performs writes (`record.match_count += 1`, `record.save`) inside a model-validation read path, causing an unconditional DB write on every validation of a matching user and unbounded counter increments from repeated failed signup attempts; validators with side effects also break under Rails' validate-on-attribute or save-without-validation paths.

[ADVISORY] db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:3-11 — Ships-inert feature: the `blocked_emails` table has no writer anywhere in the diff (no admin UI, rake task, seed path, or API), so operators cannot populate it and the blocked-email mechanism is unreachable in production; only test fabricators write to it.

[ADVISORY] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/controllers/create_account_controller.js:68-73 — the frontend pushes `result.values.email` into `rejectedEmails` for any server `errors.email`, then permanently displays `user.email.invalid` for that address; transient server-side errors (e.g. email uniqueness collision or whitelist `not_allowed` message) are converted into a wrong, permanently-cached "invalid email" verdict that never clears, and the server's precise error text is discarded in favor of the generic string.

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/users_controller.rb:194-200 — the new `errors: user.errors.to_hash` and `values: user.attributes.slice("name", "username", "email")` fields echo the user's submitted email and full name back in the JSON response on every failed signup, changing the public response contract of `POST /users` beyond what blocking emails requires (PII echo in error payloads).

[ADVISORY] app/models/user.rb:43-45 — the blocked-email check inherits the `if: :email_changed?` guard, so `BlockedEmail.should_block?` only runs when the email changed; code paths that validate/update a user without changing the email are outside the enforcement, so the invariant 'users with blocked emails cannot be saved' is only enforced on the email-change edge.

[BUG] Case-format drift between write and lookup: blocked-email matching is case-sensitive with no normalization — validator queries BlockedEmail.where(email: value) with the raw string, no before_validation downcasing, no LOWER() predicate, and no case-insensitive collation, so a blocked email with different casing registers successfully and the unique index treats A@x.com and a@x.com as distinct rows.
[BUG] Client-side rejectedEmails.contains(email) is an exact string compare, so retyping the address with different casing retries a doomed request.

[BUG] Lost-update on match_count via unguarded read-modify-write: record.match_count += 1; record.save with no increment_counter/update_all/optimistic locking, so concurrent signup attempts silently discard increments and the stat is permanently undercounted.

[ADVISORY] Ships-inert feature: no production writer for BlockedEmail anywhere in the diff — only the spec fabricator creates rows, so an operator cannot add emails to the block list and the table is permanently empty.

[ADVISORY] The if: :email_changed? guard suppresses blocked-email and domain checks on saves where email is unchanged, so paths using update_column/raw SQL or mass-assignment with the same string bypass blocking entirely.

[ADVISORY] The record.errors[attribute].blank? and BlockedEmail.should_block? short-circuit in EmailValidator means a whitelist/blacklist failure also suppresses the match-count stat update, so last_match_at/match_count under-report for emails that are also domain-restricted.

[ADVISORY] Inherited unescaped-regex domain matching: email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})", true) from raw setting text, so comma/space-separated domains match nothing and characters like '(' raise RegexpError; moving it to a shared EachValidator widens its blast radius to any model that attaches it.

[BUG] Client pushes result.values.email into rejectedEmails for ANY error on :email, not just blocked errors, permanently blacklisting emails for transient errors like 'already taken' or whitelist/blacklist errors, preventing retry.

[ADVISORY] Client displays generic I18n.t('user.email.invalid') for rejected emails instead of the server's distinct user.email.blocked message, so blocked-email users see the wrong reason on retries after the first submit.

[ADVISORY] Failure response in users_controller.rb unconditionally echoes errors hash and submitted attributes (email/name) back to anonymous signup requests, exposing reflected PII and a richer probing oracle on the public endpoint.

[ADVISORY] EmailValidator refactor moved the blocked-email check behind a guard that skips it when a domain-restriction error exists, and the check performs DB writes (record.save) during validation, so do_nothing entries still cause writes and whitelist-rejected emails never record a match.

[BUG-testing/false-confidence] spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb:16-19 — the 'doesn't add an error when email doesn't match a blocked email' test stubs should_block? to return false, so it passes even if the BlockedEmail.should_block? call were deleted from validate_each; it verifies the mock, not the code, allowing a regression that removes or inverts the BlockedEmail integration to pass green.

[ADVISORY] spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb:9-23 — the spec never triggers the whitelist/blacklist branches of validate_each (lib/validators/email_validator.rb:5-13); no test sets SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist or email_domains_blacklist, so the moved domain-restriction logic (e.g., gsub('.', '\.') escaping, if/elsif ordering) ships with zero coverage and regressions silently unblock signups.

[ADVISORY] lib/validators/email_validator.rb:17-19 — untested interaction branch: should_block? is only invoked when record.errors[attribute] is blank, so when a domain restriction error is added first, the match_count/last_match_at bookkeeping is skipped; no test exercises the combination of domain restriction failure plus a blocked email.

[ADVISORY] app/controllers/users_controller.rb:197-200 — the new response keys errors: user.errors.to_hash and values: user.attributes.slice(...) have no test; the JS client (create_account_controller.js:274-277) depends on that exact shape, so a serializer change would silently break rejectedEmails population with no failing test.

[BUG] `db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:7` — `action_type` column is `null: false` with no database default, relying only on a model `set_defaults` before_validation callback; any insert bypassing model validations (rake db:seed, bulk SQL load, raw imports) fails with a NOT NULL constraint violation — a schema drift between DB and model contracts (confidence 60, P3)

[ADVISORY] `db/migrate/20130724201552_create_blocked_emails.rb:8` — `last_match_at` and `match_count` are updated via `record.save` inside `BlockedEmail.should_block?` (`app/models/blocked_email.rb:12-15`), called from `EmailValidator` on every user validation; unauthenticated users hammering the signup endpoint drive unbounded write amplification and can inflate the counter with no rate limit (confidence 60, P2)

[ADVISORY] `app/models/blocked_email.rb:9-16` — `should_block?` performs a side-effecting `save` inside a predicate, making it non-idempotent and mutating data even when the answer is 'do_nothing'; in read-only/replica contexts the write fails and the counter increment is silently lost, producing incorrect stats under multi-DB setups (confidence 50, P3)

[ADVISORY] `app/models/user.rb:45` — the validation move causes `users#create` failure path to serialize `user.errors.to_hash` to the client (`app/controllers/users_controller.rb:197-199`), exposing internal validation error keys/messages to the browser that previously never left full_messages-joined strings (confidence 50, P3)

[BUG] `should_block?` in app/models/blocked_email.rb:13-18 performs a read-modify-write with the return value of `save` discarded; when the save fails (e.g., uniqueness race or validation failure), the match is silently dropped — match_count and last_match_at are not updated, no log is emitted, and should_block? still returns the pre-existing block decision, causing block statistics to silently undercount.

[BUG] The read-increment-write of match_count in `should_block?` is not atomic (no `match_count = match_count + 1` SQL, no lock), so two concurrent signups with the same blocked email each read the same match_count and one increment is lost even when both saves succeed.

[ADVISORY] The model validation (`validates :email, email: true`) now performs a DB write (the `BlockedEmail.save` inside `should_block?`) as a side effect of validating, so every code path calling `user.valid?` or `user.save` (admin screens, background jobs, dry-run contexts, read-only replicas) mutates the blocked_emails table, and `last_match_at` gets bumped by validation attempts that never correspond to a real signup; the `if: :email_changed?` condition means the write fires on any save where email changed, far beyond account creation.

[ADVISORY] The client-side rejection cache in create_account_controller.js:274-277 keys off `result.values.email` returned by the server, but the validity check at line 68 compares it against the raw user-typed `accountEmail`; any server-side normalization (strip/downcase) makes `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` false for the address the server just rejected, so the invalid-state marker never renders and the user can resubmit the identical rejected email repeatedly.

[ADVISORY] In create_account_controller.js:68-73, once an email lands in `rejectedEmails`, the inline validation always renders `I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` regardless of the actual server reason (e.g., 'email has already been taken' shows as 'invalid email address'), and the array is never cleared on success or retry of a different failure.

[ADVISORY] In users_controller.rb:197-201, `errors: user.errors.to_hash` is added to the failure response, but the `rescue ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` fallback branch still renders the old `{success: false, message: ...}` shape with no `errors`/`values` keys, so frontend handlers written against the new contract silently skip their logic on that path — a partial-contract rollout within the same endpoint.

goldens.comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new custom validator at lib/validators/email_validator.rb and then uses it via `validates :email, email: true` in app/models/user.rb. The diff does not show any explicit `require` or configuration change to ensure `lib/` (or `lib/validators`) is in Rails autoload/eager_load paths. Whether this becomes a production-breaking `Unknown validator: 'EmailValidator'` depends on application configuration not shown in the diff, so the claimed breakage is not verifiable here, but the review concern is real and diff-grounded: the validator loading mechanism is potentially incomplete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] should_block? performs a record.save (write plus UPDATE on every match) from inside EmailValidator#validate_each within the User model's validation phase, causing extra writes inside the User transaction; blocked-email counters/last_match_at roll back with the user save or update under contention, making stats silently wrong

adjudication.rationale: In `BlockedEmail.should_block?`, the code does a non-atomic read/modify/write (`record.match_count += 1` then `record.save`). Under concurrent signups hitting the same blocked email, increments can be lost due to race conditions; this directly affects the stored `match_count`/`last_match_at` statistics. An atomic update (e.g., `update_all` with SQL increment or `increment_counter`) would avoid this.

That makes the new blocking behavior effectively inert unless rows are inserted out-of-band, which is an incompleteness/operational concern rather than a direct correctness bug proven by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `User#email_in_restriction_setting?` and `#email_validator`, moving the logic into a new `EmailValidator` (lib/validators/email_validator.rb) and wiring it on `User` as `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?`. However, the `if: :email_changed?` guard already existed before (`validate :email_validator, if: :email_changed?`), so the whitelist/blacklist enforcement is not newly “coupled” by this change. Also, the claim that “callers validating emails outside a User record get no enforcement unless they remember the if condition” is not supported: other models could use `validates ..., email: true` without any guard. Finally, the alleged breakage from deleted `email_in_restriction_setting?` can’t be verified from this diff because no other call sites are shown.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `BlockedEmail` model/table and uses it in `EmailValidator` via `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)`, but there is no code in the diff that creates/populates `blocked_emails` (no controller/admin UI/seed/import task). As a result, in a typical deployment the feature will be ineffective unless operators manually insert rows (e.g., via DB/console). adjudication.rationale: The diff moves the domain whitelist/blacklist logic out of `User#email_validator` (removed from `app/models/user.rb`) into the new `lib/validators/email_validator.rb` (the `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist` / `email_domains_blacklist` branches and `email_in_restriction_setting?`). However, the newly added spec `spec/components/validators/email_validator_spec.rb` only exercises the `BlockedEmail.should_block?` path by stubbing it, and does not set `SiteSetting.email_domains_whitelist` or `SiteSetting.email_domains_blacklist` to test those moved branches (including the regex-building and the `if`/`elsif` precedence). adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Hidden coupling: EmailValidator in lib/ hard-depends on the BlockedEmail model, executing DB reads and writes (match_count increment, last_match_at update, save) from inside validate_each on every email validation, even when action_type is :do_nothing or the email later fails uniqueness, inflating match counts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EmailValidator#validate_each` calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` (lib/validators/email_validator.rb), which performs a DB lookup and, if a `BlockedEmail` record exists, increments `match_count`, sets `last_match_at`, and `save`s regardless of `action_type` (app/models/blocked_email.rb). This is tight coupling and causes DB writes during validation even when `action_type` is `:do_nothing` (explicitly tested in spec/models/blocked_email_spec.rb) and regardless of whether other validators (e.g., uniqueness) later prevent the user from being created. However, because the specs assert stats update even for `:do_nothing`, the “inflating match counts” aspect looks like a product/architecture concern rather than a clear defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] rejectedEmails is only populated when result.errors.email is present, and when a blocked email is paired with other errors the user sees the generic 'user.email.invalid' message instead of the distinct 'user.email.blocked' locale string this diff adds but never uses on the client.

adjudication.rationale: In create_account_controller.js, once an email is pushed into `rejectedEmails`, `emailValidation` always returns `failed: true` with `reason: I18n.t('user.email.invalid')` (see the new `contains(email)` block). The server-side change introduces a distinct blocked-email error message (`user.email.blocked`) via the new EmailValidator and locale key, but the client never inspects `result.errors.email` to choose that message; it only uses presence of `result.errors.email` to push into `rejectedEmails`, then shows the generic `user.email.invalid` on subsequent validation for that email. Thus blocked emails (even when accompanied by other errors) will be presented as “invalid” in the field-level validation instead of “blocked”.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds blocked-email enforcement inside a new `EmailValidator`, which is invoked via `validates :email, email: true, if: :email_changed?` in `User` (app/models/user.rb). adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `EmailValidator` which calls `BlockedEmail.should_block?(value)` during validation (`lib/validators/email_validator.rb:12-14`). `should_block?` does mutate-and-save (`record.match_count += 1`, `record.last_match_at = ...`, `record.save`) whenever a matching `BlockedEmail` exists (`app/models/blocked_email.rb:11-16`). The `emailValidation` computed property then short-circuits on `rejectedEmails.contains(email)` and returns `{failed: true, reason: I18n.t('user.email.invalid')}`. adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Lost-update on match_count via unguarded read-modify-write: record.match_count += 1; record.save with no increment_counter/update_all/optimistic locking, so concurrent signup attempts silently discard increments and the stat is permanently undercounted.

With concurrent calls matching the same `blocked_emails.email`, increments can be lost because two processes can read the same `match_count` and both write back `+1`, undercounting `match_count` (and potentially racing on `last_match_at`).
